statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of five public archetypes. Authenticated editor, checkout completion, localized variants and every template URL were out of scope.

page.notes: Public marketing/listing/detail pages redirect by locale and hydrate into a large React-like experience. No authenticated editor source was available.

Commercial decision page; represents plan comparison, pricing clarity and account conversion.
Support/search surface; represents recovery and self-service help.
Invalid sitemap URL response was inspected as a representative not-found recovery state; it offered a home link and error identifier.

findings.summary: The public landing page does not adapt to the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-identical in appearance to the light capture, and the structure probe reports computed colorScheme “light”.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and map surfaces/text through light-dark() or prefers-color-scheme tokens.

findings.summary: Continuous hero motion remains active when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, getAnimations() returned 42 running animations, each with 1400 ms duration and an infinite iteration count (serialized as null).
findings.suggestedFix: Use prefers-reduced-motion to remove non-essential loops and replace motion with a static composition.

findings.summary: The first-load cookie panel obscures most of the primary content on every sampled marketing page.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show the cookie panel covering roughly half the viewport and hiding the primary call to action/content on home, templates, presentation and pricing pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-preserving consent surface where legally possible while keeping accept, reject and manage choices equally available.

findings.summary: The blocking consent overlay is not exposed with a native dialog or popover primitive.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM contains zero dialog and zero popover elements while the screenshot shows a blocking overlay.
findings.suggestedFix: Model blocking consent as a properly labelled dialog with managed focus, or a non-modal popover when blocking is unnecessary.

findings.summary: The mobile templates listing has poor visual stability.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 layout observer measured CLS 0.2157, including a 0.21285 shift at about 6.18 seconds, above the 0.1 good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for late template/list content and identify the element injected at ~6.18 s; give media and async regions explicit intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: Throttled load performance misses the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.168 s, FCP 3.31 s and TTI 7.241 s; the first-party trace corroborated two long tasks and 92.97 ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP request chain, prioritize the hero/LCP resource, and defer non-critical scripts and styles.

findings.summary: The anonymous homepage ships a large amount of avoidable code and network weight.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 60 requests and 3.27 MB transferred; Lighthouse estimated 277 KiB unused JavaScript and 62 KiB unused CSS, with four individual JS resources around 31–61% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split anonymous marketing code, conditionally load editor/account dependencies, remove unused CSS, and defer Google identity until sign-in intent.

findings.summary: Homepage imagery is not delivered responsively or with stable intrinsic sizing.
findings.evidence: The image probe found all 13 images without width/height, 11 without srcset, 8 below-fold images not lazy-loaded and 9 legacy-format assets; Lighthouse independently failed the unsized-images audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width/height, srcset/sizes, lazy loading below the fold, and AVIF/WebP variants for raster assets.

findings.summary: Deprecated unload handling prevents back/forward cache restoration.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found an unload listener in sentry_browser.js and four BFCache failure reasons, including the unload handler and no-store responses.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unload listeners in favor of pagehide/visibilitychange and audit no-store use so eligible public pages can enter BFCache.

findings.summary: Browser security policy and cookie posture have avoidable gaps.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found CSP unsafe-eval and no Permissions-Policy. Cookie inspection found g_state without Secure and four of five cookies flagged, including SameSite=None cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-eval through compatible bundling, add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, secure g_state, and restrict SameSite=None to cookies that truly require cross-site use.

findings.summary: Core public content is largely absent from raw server HTML.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 4% raw/rendered word coverage on home, 2% on templates and 4% on the presentation page; each was classified as a JS shell and raw HTML lacked title and h1.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render or statically emit each landing page’s title, h1, primary copy, links and template/product content, then hydrate enhancements.

findings.summary: Public content and primary discovery journeys do not progressively enhance without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Raw HTML comparisons across three representative public templates retained only 2–4% of rendered words and omitted title/h1, despite the pages having substantial public content.
findings.suggestedFix: Ship meaningful HTML for navigation, headings, copy and template links; use client JavaScript to enhance search/filter/editor entry rather than create the content baseline.

findings.summary: Repeated navigation-menu toggling produced substantial retained-heap growth.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary was 67.15 MB across 1.52M nodes; after 20 menu toggles it was 88.60 MB across 2.06M nodes, about 32% more bytes and 36% more nodes. Separate page sessions add variance, so this is a leak signal requiring allocation-retainer confirmation.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat baseline/target/final snapshots in one session, force GC, inspect retainers for menu DOM/listeners, and release transient navigation state after close.

findings.summary: The initial memory footprint is disproportionate for a marketing landing page.
findings.evidence: A post-load heap summary contained about 1.52M heap nodes, 8.77M edges and 67.15 MB self size before entering the editor.
findings.suggestedFix: Use heap allocation profiles to remove anonymous-page editor/runtime state, delay optional features, and set a landing-page heap budget.

findings.summary: State and route changes do not expose View Transition styling on the sampled public pages.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition-name or ::view-transition usage across the homepage snapshot, while the page presents carousels, menus and cross-page journeys.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for major menu/carousel state and cross-document transitions for compatible marketing routes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Canva’s agent-relevant productivity capabilities are not exposed as structured browser tools.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no WebMCP/model-context registration on the public product surface; agents must infer actions from a large rendered UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Pilot narrowly scoped WebMCP tools or agentic forms for safe tasks such as template search and draft creation, with explicit confirmation for consequential actions.
